questions.q: What is Azure Event Hubs' Kafka-compatible endpoint, per this lesson?
options: A protocol-level bridge that lets real Kafka client code connect to Event Hubs, often with just a connection-string and port change
A full open-source reimplementation of every Kafka feature including Connect and Streams
A tool that converts Kafka topics into Azure SQL tables automatically
A separate product entirely unrelated to Azure Event Hubs
questions.explain: It's a compatibility layer on top of Event Hubs' native API, not a separate Kafka distribution.

questions.q: What actually has to change in an existing Kafka producer/consumer application to point it at Event Hubs instead of a real broker?
options: Configuration only — the broker address and authentication mechanism — not the producer/consumer application logic itself
The Kafka client library must be replaced with an Azure-specific SDK
Nothing at all needs to change, including configuration
The entire application must be rewritten from scratch in a different language
questions.explain: The same KafkaProducer/KafkaConsumer classes and send()/poll() calls are used — only bootstrap.servers and the SASL_SSL auth config change.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which part of Kafka compatibility is only partially supported by Event Hubs?
options: The basic consumer poll() call
The Kafka Admin API — some administrative operations instead go through Azure's own control plane
The basic producer send() call
TCP networking itself
questions.explain: Not every Admin API call available against a self-hosted cluster or Confluent Cloud has a direct Event Hubs equivalent.

questions.q: Why isn't it guaranteed that Kafka Connect, Kafka Streams, or ksqlDB will work the same way against Event Hubs as against real Kafka?
options: Kafka Connect, Streams, and ksqlDB don't exist as concepts
This limitation only affects Confluent Cloud, not Event Hubs
Event Hubs runs a full copy of Kafka Connect automatically for every namespace
Those tools are built expecting a real Kafka-protocol-speaking cluster underneath, and Event Hubs' compatibility layer doesn't guarantee full support across that whole ecosystem
questions.explain: Some connectors work against the endpoint, but it isn't a blanket guarantee the way it is on real Kafka or Confluent Cloud.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect to Terraform & Bicep Lesson 10?
options: Lesson 10 covers actually provisioning the Event Hub resource with infrastructure as code; this lesson covers what you can point existing Kafka client code at once that resource exists
Lesson 10 replaces the need to learn Kafka's Admin API
There is no connection between the two lessons
Terraform & Bicep Lesson 10 is about deploying Kafka Streams applications
questions.explain: The provisioning step and the client-compatibility step are two different, complementary parts of using Event Hubs with Kafka tooling.
